**Development — no registry entry. Independent review pending. Physical promotion 0.** This executes the first WBS batch at specification and small-instance level. The acceptance contract is a constructor's development design rule, not a custodian promotion or measured specification. It preserves M8–M10 and the unmodified ledger/governance attachments. There is no complete autonomous pair-qubit controller or native preparation result.

# 1. WBS 1.1: define the target and retain the whole domain

The selected endpoint is WBS D2: a supplied finite autonomous controller implementing the retained production/capture/donor-renewal semantics, with an admitted pair-qubit architecture. D1, the externally scheduled full supplied controller, remains an intermediate target. Native origin and physical qualification remain additional gates.

Retain M8's entire source/output/donor bank, every individual fuel factor, reference, flag, attempt record, END and original global address clock Q. The retained instance uses 380 binary encoding factors under M9's support-wise extension policy. Any **new** scheduling timer C, program, mediator, ancillary or quantum control-reservoir factor is additional; do not rename or discard Q to hide it. Padding and arbitrary admitted spectators Y also remain in the comparison domain.

The semantic bank target is the retained M7/M8 completed-bank target at the same declared parameter t, including old reference correlations and the unused final module. Define the auxiliary target state chi_A(t) before executing a candidate: it must come from an explicit reference evolution/program-resource specification, not from tracing the candidate's actual output. The enlarged target has form
\[
\rho_{\rm target}(t)=J\rho^{M8}_{\rm semantic}(t)J^{\dagger}
\otimes\chi_A(t),
\]
with spectator correlations carried by the specified semantic map. Product separation here deliberately requires a certified debit for undesired work/auxiliary correlations. If resources are consumed, their named final states belong in chi_A; a clean or reusable timer is not assumed.

The semantic guarantee remains scoped to the admitted ready-bank input class and full-joint preparation defects used by the retained source theorem. It is not promoted to all arbitrary source states. Exact unitary implementation comparisons may be uniform on the full encoded space and arbitrary spectator extensions; the toy below has that stronger work-input statement. Postselection, output-only trace distance and discarded padding cannot replace the complete comparison.

# 2. WBS 1.2: define the permitted architecture

For the intended binary realization, the complete post-launch Hermitian generator must be constant and decompose as onsite and two-qubit terms on the named tensor factors. All backgrounds and timer-conditioning interactions count. Auxiliary binary factors and changed encodings are allowed only when explicitly named and included in the state/resource certificate. Arbitrary abstract pair connectivity is allowed at this development stage; geometric locality is not claimed.

Initial preparation is supplied. After launch there is no external pulse timestamp, classical switching schedule, hidden reset, measurement-conditioned renewal, or discarded control reservoir. A native ready-bank law is not inferred. Approximate mediator/encoded realizations are permitted only with full finite-time error, leakage, preparation and correlation costs. No infinite coupling, unbounded ancillary reservoir or uncharged effective projection is admitted.

For each candidate, predeclare finite resource limits N_max (all binary factors), h_max (each grouped onsite/pair control term), J_max (sum of term norms), energy spread and initial preparation cost, as well as the observation interval. Group terms on each support before stating the cap; splitting a large term into many small ones cannot evade it. These numerical limits for the full controller are **not yet sized**. That unresolved envelope is part of WBS 1.3, so this release does not mark the entire first phase complete.

The comparator toy below deliberately uses one three-address register and one binary work factor. It is pair-supported as a **register** construction. Its binary encoding is then audited against the stricter intended qubit definition. Neither result changes M8's fixed-factor theorem.

# 3. WBS 1.3: specify the complete acceptance predicate

Keep the retained comparison scale kappa_0=4096; it is an engineered development parameter, not calibrated proper time. The requested full-controller completion is T_0=pi/8192, with the M8 retention interval [pi/12288,pi/6144]. The candidate must compare at actual elapsed time tau=t across that interval, or charge the complete semantic-time difference. A separate circuit selected for each t is not an autonomous retention certificate.

Use complete trace distance with the one-half convention. The selected sufficient threshold is 11/100, matching the retained example. Its inherited outward certificate B8 already owns the original source semantic, native-bare comparison, clock tail and phase debits under the original ideal preparation/implementation assumptions. A revised source assumption requires revising B8; its confidence does not improve by another citation.

Reserve an additional total 1/1000, provisionally partitioned as follows. These are acceptance allocations, **not certified errors** and not new UD coefficients.

| Additional debit | Allocation | Must cover |
|---|---:|---|
| Digital approximation | 1/5000 | Any finite product-formula or corresponding encoded-channel approximation |
| Realization/control | 1/5000 | Full implementation defect, background or finite mediator approximation |
| Timer and correlations | 1/5000 | Autonomous timing mismatch and work/auxiliary correlation comparison |
| New encoding/preparation | 1/5000 | Additional encoding, auxiliary readiness and preparation defects |
| Semantic elapsed time | 1/5000 | Full target difference when actual elapsed and logical time differ |

Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies B8+1/1000<11/100. Every comparison must be defined in a telescoping chain so that the same defect is charged once. Timer timing can reside in the timer debit or a channel-realization debit, not both; the final semantic-time debit compares different target times. The original epsilon_F is already in B8. Moving budget between categories requires a versioned contract amendment and a new outward total, not convenient relabeling after a failed check.

Acceptance requires the complete budget and each resource limit to hold over the declared interval, with finite reserves and correct failure/exhaustion semantics. A sufficient bound exceeding the threshold is a failed certificate; it is not automatically a lower bound on actual error. A direct full-state counterexample is stronger and must be recorded. Since the full numerical resource envelope and new debit proofs remain open, full-controller feasibility is **not established** here.

# 4. WBS 4.1–4.2: a supplied finite autonomous comparator

Let C have addresses 0,1,2 and B be a binary work factor with degenerate bare energy. Supply initial C=|0>. The gate word is X followed chronologically by Z, so its completed product is ZX; these gates do not commute. Define prefixes P_0=I, P_1=X, P_2=ZX and
\[
W=\sum_{j=0}^{2}|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes P_j,
\quad
H_C=\sqrt2\kappa_C(|1\rangle\langle0|+|2\rangle\langle1|+\mathrm{adjoints}),
\]
\[
H_{CB}=W(H_C\otimes I)W^{\dagger}
=\sqrt2\kappa_C(|1\rangle\langle0|\otimes X
+|2\rangle\langle1|\otimes Z+\mathrm{adjoints}).
\]
The scale kappa_C of this toy is distinct from kappa_0 of the full retained controller. This uses the previously retained spin-clock/prefix-dressing method as a small comparator; no new universal clock method or priority claim is made. All couplings are constant after launch. No external pulse schedule drives the ordering.

**Theorem M11.1 (finite autonomous noncommuting word).** For every work input, including entanglement with a spectator, at $T_C=\pi/(2\kappa_C)$,
\[
e^{-iT_C H_{CB}}|0\rangle|\psi\rangle
=-|2\rangle ZX|\psi\rangle.
\]
At $2T_C=\pi/\kappa_C$, the full unitary returns to identity. The full generator norm is $2\kappa_C$. The supplied initial clock has energy mean zero and variance $2\kappa_C^2$.

*Proof.* Conjugation by the unitary W gives exact dressed propagation. H_C is the n=2 spin clock: its eigenvalues are $-2\kappa_C,0,2\kappa_C$, and its transfer at T_C maps |0> to -|2>. Since P_0=I and P_2=ZX, dressing gives the stated full-input map. All three eigenphases return to one at 2T_C. Norm and initial variance follow from the spectrum and the first edge amplitude $\sqrt2\kappa_C$. Tensoring a spectator preserves the identity. $\square$

This establishes ordered computation from a supplied finite state. It does not establish native timer formation or a permanent record. Reversible return undoes the completed word; no reservoir is silently renewed.

# 5. WBS 4.3: endpoint correctness does not give a retention plateau

At t=T_C/2 and work input |0>, the dressed state has work probabilities 1/4 and 3/4. Its reduced-work purity is 5/8, demonstrating clock/work entanglement. Compare with the completed work state ZX|0> and the freely propagated clock reference. The work marginal trace distance is 1/4, whereas the **full** pure-state trace distance is sqrt(15)/4. Thus a favorable marginal does not certify the requested joint target.

On the comparator interval $[\pi/(3\kappa_C),2\pi/(3\kappa_C)]$, the unfinished-prefix tail is R=1-(3/4)^2=7/16 at the endpoints. The retained full-target tail bound is $2\sqrt{R(1-R)}=3\sqrt7/8$. For this work input, the actual joint error at the left endpoint is
\[
D=\frac{\sqrt{247}}{16}>\frac{11}{100}.
\]
Indeed the target/actual overlap is 3/16 there, giving D squared=247/256. This is an actual counterexample to that toy meeting the selected uniform window threshold, not merely a conservative-bound failure. Identity padding and a larger clock may improve a window but change dimension, energy and support costs; that work remains open.

# 6. WBS 5.1: direct binary encoding has an exact locality gap

Encode clock addresses 0,1,2 as binary labels 00,01,11, with 10 padding. Let J embed C tensor B into the resulting three-qubit space and use zero extension on this clock/work support. In qubit order C_0,C_1,B,
\[
K=JH_{CB}J^{\dagger}
=\frac{\kappa_C}{\sqrt2}(IXX+ZXX+XIZ-XZZ).
\]
The first edge changes the low clock bit and B conditional on the high bit being zero. The second changes the high clock bit, applies Z to B, and requires the low bit to be one. These conditions create the weight-three strings ZXX and XZZ. Gray labeling reduces changed bits; it does not remove conditional support.

**Theorem M11.2 (best direct two-qubit generator defect).** On this fixed full eight-dimensional encoded space,
\[
\inf_{K_2\ \mathrm{sum\ of\ onsite/pair\ terms}}
\|K-K_2\|=\kappa_C.
\]

*Proof.* Every such Hermitian K_2 has only Pauli strings of weight at most two. Orthogonality of the Pauli basis leaves weight-three coefficients $+\kappa_C/\sqrt2$ on ZXX and $-\kappa_C/\sqrt2$ on XZZ in K-K_2. Its normalized squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm is therefore at least $\kappa_C^2$; operator norm is at least this root. The two weight-three strings anticommute and each squares to identity. Choosing $K_2=(\kappa_C/\sqrt2)(IXX+XIZ)$ leaves a residual whose square is $\kappa_C^2 I$. Its operator norm is exactly kappa_C, attaining the lower bound. $\square$

This concerns direct equality or uniform generator comparison for this explicit full-space Gray encoding and extension. It is not an impossibility theorem for other encodings, auxiliary factors, approximate effective designs or final unitaries. An onsite Y rotation alone can implement the work product ZX at one endpoint, while reproducing neither this clock trajectory nor its full joint dynamics. The replay includes that negative control.

The direct norm-defect Duhamel debit at the comparator interval's upper time is at least $2\pi/3$, so the same-generator sufficient bound is vacuous after capping trace distance at one. This does not prove every finite-time two-qubit approximation is inaccurate. It shows that the selected direct-small-generator-defect route cannot meet the contract.
